ImageDescription.value: This photograph appears to commemorate the day Asa Griggs Candler purchased the remaining shares to Coca Cola Company from Dr. Pemberton, who died a few months later on August 16, 1888. This photograph was commissioned by Candler and taken by Kuhns' Photo to make a record of the historic occasion. However, in 1910, Candler ordered all corporate documents pertaining to this first Coca Cola incorporation, burned; further obscuring its origins. Candler did retain one copy of this iconic photographic image for himself, as his own personal property, and not property/ documents of the original Coca Cola Company he had ordered burned in 1910. Thus, this image shown, represents the only extant original copy that remains in the world.

DateTimeOriginal.value: Originally created in the year 1888. Taken at 47 Peachtree Street, Atlanta, GA. First publication of this exact original photograph, from a cropped copy supplied to the printer, of this exact and only extant original photograph of this image, was 1950/04/15.

Artist.value:
Original photographer in 1888 was "KUHNS' Photo" of "Atlanta, GA." The JPG image hereof shows first ever release of the full original image (that was lost for over fifty years), recently discovered and finally fully verified as being the only extant example, by RICHARD WARREN LIPACK, author. Information on computer files at Emory University, Atlanta, GA. dated March / April 2012, between RICHARD WARREN LIPACK and the Manuscript, Archives and Rare Book Library at Emory University, Atlanta, GA., corroborates that the original photograph from 1888 owned by RICHARD WARREN LIPACK was once the personal property of ASA GRIGGS CANDLER (who appears in the photograph along with Dr. John Stith Pemberton - the original inventor of Coca Cola), with full original mount showing the name "Kuhns' Photo.," of which a later mid-20th century copy Kodak "Velox" silver-bromide photograph (without photographer attribution), was taken from this original (the same original now uploaded to Wikipedia), that was published on page 68 in the book ASA GRIGGS CANDLER by CHARLES HOWARD CANDLER in 1950 by Emory University, Atlanta, GA. The original "1888 Asa G. Candler & Co." mounted albumen photograph, as of this date of uploading, is owned by RICHARD WARREN LIPACK. Such ownership is documented between RICHARD WARREN LIPACK and Research and Public Services Archivist Sara J. Logue of the Manuscript, Archives and Rare Book Library, which represents the Candler family archives thereof, at Emory University, Atlanta, Georgia. Reference archivists at the Manuscript, Archives , and Rare Book Library at Emory University believe that the "1888 Asa G. Candler & Co." photograph discovered by RICHARD WARREN LIPACK to be the same one reproduced in Candler's son's 1950 tome.

Also as a matter of record, ownership by RICHARD WARREN LIPACK of the original "1888 Asa G. Candler & Co." albumen photograph is recorded and on file with the legal department of The Coca-Cola Company, Atlanta, Georgia.

This is a scene showing the newly installed "Boat Motor" styled Coca-Cola soda dispenser just after the dispenser's installation at Fleeman's Pharmacy, Atlanta, Georgia, circa 1948. The legend is that this "Boat Motor" styled Coca-Cola dispenser was the first ever of this 1948 model installed anywhere, and in this case was installed in the city where Coca-Cola was created.

The pharmacy was originally built in 1914 under the name Atkins Park Pharmacy and in the 1930's became known as Cox & Baucom; all in an era that came to be called “the golden age of soda fountains."

From its very onset in 1914, the pharmacy began to serve Coca-Cola, and when it closed it's doors in 1995, it had gained the distinction of being the longest-running establishment anywhere to have served Coca-Cola — having served Coca-Cola from the same location for eighty-one years straight.

Jack Fleeman took over the pharmacy from Messrs. Cox & Baucom. During its existence, Fleeman's Pharmacy became basically the very first Coca-Cola museum, and the walls of the establishment featured rare Coca-Cola artifacts from years past. Some of the Candler family, descendants of Coca-Cola founder Asa Griggs Candler, had been known to sometimes visit with Jack Fleeman over the years, and it has been said, that sometimes they would gift Jack Fleeman some old Coca-Cola mementos passed down through the Candler family for his pharmacy museum.

The photograph shows two 'soda jerks,' a name given to young teenagers who worked in commercial establishments that served carbonated soda products of years gone by.

177961896.title: File:St. John Chrysostom Melkite Catholic Church on Ponce de Leon Avenue in Atlanta.jpg

ImageDescription.value:
St. John Chrysostom Melkite Catholic Church on Ponce de Leon Avenue in Atlanta, seen here, did not begin as a church. Before its "present and holy utilization," as described on the church's website, the building was the home of Coca-Cola magnate Asa Griggs Candler.

Built in 1916 at a cost of $210,000, it remained in the Candler family long after his death in 1929. After years of being rented out and used as boarding home, the structure was bought in 1946 by the American Legion with the intention of using it for their state headquarter, a plan which did not materialize.

Atlanta's small Melkite Catholic Community purchased the former Candler mansion in 1957 for $62,000. It took more than $250,000, though, "to transform it, as much as possible, into the beginning of a proper Byzantine house of worship."

177736140.title: File:View of the downtown Atlanta skyline looking south along Peachtree Street from the plaza of the Georgia Pacific Tower.jpg

ImageDescription.value: View of the downtown Atlanta skyline looking south along Peachtree Street from the plaza of the Georgia Pacific Tower. The 17-story Candler Building, completed in 1906 by Coca-Cola magnate Asa Griggs Candler, is on the left. Across Peachtree from it is Marriott's 21-story Residence Inn Atlanta Downtown occupying what originally was the Rhodes-Haverty Building. Just behind it is the 32-story Equitable Building. In the lower portion of the center of the frame is the Flatiron Building. Built in 1897, the Flatiron Building is Atlanta's oldest standing skyscraper.
